facts.label: Leverage trajectory and drivers
facts.text: Leverage on the company's own debt definition fell in two steps. Total debt, which is long-term debt net of financing costs and excludes finance leases, went from USD 917.5 million at September 30, 2024 to USD 832.2 million a year later and USD 716.6 million at June 30, 2026, while last-twelve-month reported EBITDA moved from negative USD 13.7 million in fiscal 2024 to USD 118.0 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 216.6 million. Reported EBITDA carries non-cash charges, USD 191.0 million of impairments in fiscal 2024 and USD 53.7 million in fiscal 2025, so reported leverage is not calculable for fiscal 2024 and is 7.05x for fiscal 2025. Taking only the fiscal 2025 impairment out of EBITDA would give 4.85x, so about 2.20x of the 3.74x fall to 3.31x is that charge leaving the base, and the rest is debt paydown and earnings growth. On the issuer-adjusted measure, which adds the charges back, gross leverage was 4.45x, 4.19x and 3.07x and net leverage at June 30, 2026 is 2.83x, matching the company's own 2.8x. Creditors should therefore anchor on adjusted leverage near 3x and reported leverage near 3.3x, and treat any reading of a seven-turn improvement as an artefact of the base year. facts.text: Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 1.99x in fiscal 2025 and 5.21x over the last twelve months, but the second figure overstates cover. facts.label: Liquidity and maturity profile
facts.text: Liquidity is USD 328.1 million at June 30, 2026 (cash USD 56.3 million plus USD 271.8 million of undrawn revolver), against USD 364.6 million at September 30, 2025 and USD 189.9 million at September 30, 2024. The revolver (commitments of USD 325.0 million, borrowings of USD 35.0 million and letters of credit of USD 18.2 million) falls due in May 2028, about 22 months after the balance sheet date, and is the nearest maturity; the AR facility's USD 43.0 million follows in March 2029 and the USD 650.0 million 2030 notes after that, which is 89.29% of principal. No principal is due in fiscal 2026 or fiscal 2027. Refinancing risk is therefore not near, but one bullet carries almost nine-tenths of the debt and the revolver is the only committed backstop. The AR facility's undrawn capacity (up to USD 100.0 million, subject to conditions, with USD 43.0 million drawn) is not stated and is excluded, and USD 14.5 million of the cash is held by foreign subsidiaries. The 2030 notes become callable at 104.0% of principal from July 1, 2027, falling to par on or after July 1, 2029, so a refinancing before 2029 would carry a call premium of up to 4.0%. facts.label: Data quality and definition risks
facts.text: Management reports material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting that are still being remediated, and the auditor gave an adverse opinion on internal control at September 30, 2024 and September 30, 2025, so the figures carry a reliability risk even though the auditor's opinion on the fiscal 2025 statements says they present fairly. The cross-checks that could be run agree: fiscal 2024 sales, net loss, EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and total debt are the same in the 2024 and 2025 annual reports, and the nine-month and quarter figures in the June 2026 quarterly report agree with the third-quarter release for sales, operating income, net income, EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and net debt. The differences found are presentational: finance leases moved to their own balance sheet lines and a term loan repayment was reclassified inside financing cash flows. Three debt bases coexist for one date (total debt of USD 716.6 million, principal of USD 728.0 million and carrying value with finance leases of USD 728.1 million), and the covenant tests use first lien debt at principal and a consolidated EBITDA that may include run-rate cost savings, neither of which is supplied, so no headroom is computed. The 2030 notes carry two maturity dates and two cost figures in the filings, and the debt table captions senior notes as subordinated, which is why ranking follows the notes' own description. limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- The latest statements are for June 30, 2026, 141 days before the as-of date, and no annual report, fourth-quarter release or later filing for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 is supplied, so every balance and ratio is stated at June 30, 2026, the seasonal low for working-capital needs, and year-end net debt and leverage are not established. Severity: Medium. Closing action: supply the fiscal 2026 annual report and fourth-quarter release. - Covenant compliance and headroom after December 31, 2025 are not established: the filings print no compliance statement or ratio for March 31 or June 30, 2026 and the covenant EBITDA definition, which can include run-rate cost savings, is not supplied, so no covenant figure is computed. Severity: Medium. Closing action: supply the executed credit agreement and compliance certificates. - Material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting remain under remediation and disclosure controls were ineffective at June 30, 2026, which limits reliance on any single source; the cross-checks run found no numerical disagreement. Severity: Medium. Closing action: read the remediation status in the fiscal 2026 annual report. - Fiscal 2024 total debt / EBITDA and net debt / EBITDA on reported EBITDA are not calculable because reported EBITDA is negative USD 13.7 million; the adjusted ratios stand beside them. Severity: Low. Closing action: none possible, since the sign of the denominator is reported. - Statement lines that print a dash are held as missing values, not zero. Income statement: loss on impairments and other operating (income) expense in the nine months and third quarter of 2026, loss on extinguishment of debt in fiscal 2024 and the third quarter of 2026, and loss on sale of business in the nine months and third quarter of 2025. Cash flow: loss on extinguishment, impairments, contingent consideration remeasurement, loss on disposition, change in other assets, sale proceeds, 2030 and 2027 notes lines, dividends and contingent consideration payments in the periods where the statement shows a dash or has no line. Balance sheet: current portion of long-term debt at September 30, 2025 and income taxes payable at June 30, 2026. These are nil or inapplicable in the period on the face of the statement and affect completeness, not any total. Severity: Low. Closing action: none needed beyond the filings. - Segment Adjusted EBITDA for fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025 is not printed in the annual report, and Corporate and Other Adjusted EBITDA is not printed in any source read, so the segment earnings trend over a full year is not established. Severity: Low. Closing action: supply the fiscal 2025 fourth-quarter release or a segment reconciliation. - The AR facility's interest rate, rate type, reference rate, spread, legal rank and undrawn capacity are not stated, so its USD 43.0 million is left out of the ranked debt stack and its unused capacity (committed up to USD 100.0 million, subject to conditions) is excluded from liquidity. Severity: Medium. Closing action: supply the receivables financing agreement. - The revolver's margin grid, floors and any scheduled repayments are not stated (only a weighted average rate of about 5.8% at June 30, 2026), and instrument-level carrying values are not stated (the note gives principal by instrument and one financing cost of USD 11.4 million), so the debt instruments table carries principal with a separate financing-cost line. Severity: Low. Closing action: supply the credit agreement. - The 2030 notes mature on June 16, 2030 in the 2025 annual report and on July 1, 2030 in the three 2026 quarterly reports, with financing costs of USD 13.0 million in the annual report and two quarterly reports and USD 13.3 million in the June 2026 report; both dates fall in fiscal 2030 and the ladder is unaffected. Severity: Low. Closing action: supply the indenture. - The debt table captions the 2030 notes and the AR facility as subordinated debt while the notes are described as senior unsecured, and the redeemed 2027 notes were described as subordinated; ranking follows the notes' own description and the AR facility's rank is not established. Severity: Low. Closing action: supply the indenture and intercreditor documents. - The guarantor subsidiaries of the 2030 notes are not named and no security documents are supplied, so structural priority is read only from the filings' summaries. Severity: Medium. Closing action: supply the indenture and security documents. - Cash interest paid over the last twelve months (USD 41.6 million) holds one coupon on the 2030 notes and sits below interest expense (USD 67.9 million), so cover on cash interest overstates cover on expense until two coupons fall in a twelve-month window. Severity: Low. Closing action: re-measure after the fiscal 2026 annual report. - Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not stated; only total capital expenditure is, so discretionary spending is not established. Severity: Low. Closing action: management disclosure. - Fiscal 2023 and earlier years are not carried as statement columns; fiscal 2023 amounts appear only as comparatives in the supplied annual reports and the Form 10-K/A that carried the earlier restatement is not supplied. Severity: Low. Closing action: supply it if a longer history is needed. - The fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 is not reported discretely and is derived as the year less nine months, so its sales of USD 227.5 million and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 41.6 million are not issuer-reported. Severity: Low. Closing action: supply the fiscal 2025 fourth-quarter release. - The balance sheet at June 30, 2025 is not among the statements read, so liquidity for the nine months of 2025 is not supplied in the dashboard. Severity: Low. Closing action: supply the June 2025 quarterly report. - Operating lease liabilities of USD 46.5 million sit in other liabilities outside Total Debt, and the UK pension plan was overfunded by USD 1.2 million at September 30, 2025 with no update at June 30, 2026. Severity: Low. Closing action: none needed for leverage; note for fixed-charge analysis. - The July 20, 2026 tariff announcement is described but its effect is not quantified and no net debt figure changes. Severity: Low. Closing action: monitor in the fiscal 2026 annual report.

Highway deicing volumes rose 20.41% in fiscal 2025 on a more normal winter and fell 2.54% in the nine months to June 2026, while the average highway price rose 7.80%. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against caution is that, in management's words, salt has no known cost-effective alternative for most high-volume uses, that no customer reached 10% of sales in any of the last three fiscal years, that highway prices rose 7.80% in the nine months to June 2026 and management describes the coming highway bid season as constructive, and that Plant Nutrition earnings have recovered. Management also reports a stronger-than-average winter in fiscal 2026. These support a view that the business is steadier than its weather exposure suggests. The view would improve if the next winter is average and the fiscal 2027 volume decline management expects is mild, if remediation of the control weaknesses is reported complete, and if Goderich production costs fall. It would worsen if a mine or labour disruption hits Goderich, if the tariffs announced for August 2026 reach Canadian salt exports, or if the board reverses the dividend suspension before debt is lower. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: No new debt issue or acquisition is reported after June 30, 2026 in the documents read. The transactions that shape the creditor position are all earlier. On June 16, 2025 the company issued USD 650.0 million of 8.00% senior unsecured notes due 2030 and used the proceeds to repay the revolver and term loan in full and to redeem USD 350.0 million of its 6.75% notes due 2027; the same day a fifth amendment fixed revolver commitments at USD 325.0 million and reset the financial covenants to a first lien leverage test and an interest coverage test. On March 30, 2026 it redeemed the remaining USD 150.0 million of the 2027 notes at par from cash, and on March 19, 2026 it extended its receivables financing facility to March 2029. On March 1, 2026 it sold the Wynyard sulfate of potash business for total consideration of about USD 30.8 million, receiving USD 23.3 million of net cash and booking a USD 14.5 million loss, of which USD 13.1 million is non-cash. In 2025 it exited the Fortress fire retardant business it had bought in 2023, selling the assets for USD 20.0 million, and in January 2024 it ended its lithium project after an impairment of USD 74.8 million. For creditors, the sequence moved the company from secured bank debt and subordinated notes to a structure dominated by one unsecured bond due 2030, with a small revolver and receivables facility, removed near-term maturities and stopped capital going to projects outside salt and sulfate of potash. facts.label: Overall governance view
facts.text: Overall, Compass Minerals presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is the suspension of dividends in April 2024 and the use of asset-sale proceeds and cash to retire notes, which matters because it keeps cash in the business and lowers refinancing exposure, and implies a financial policy aligned with creditors. Countervailing evidence is the unremediated control weaknesses, a restatement, a notice of default in September 2024 for a late quarterly report that was cured, and a management team in which every listed officer took the current post since January 2024. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit agreement and indenture, and the fiscal 2026 annual report. The review is complete with limitations at a Medium risk level. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. The first strength is a low-cost, high-scale salt franchise. The Goderich mine is described as the largest underground rock salt mine in the world, with a deep-water port, and the company has logistics depots close to its customers, so delivered cost is competitive in a product where freight is a large part of price; this lowers the risk of losing tenders and supports volume through weak winters. The second strength is near-term refinancing safety: no principal falls due before May 2028 and liquidity is USD 328.1 million, so a poor quarter can be absorbed without a financing event. The third is financial policy: dividends are suspended and disposal proceeds and cash retired the 2027 notes, so cash accrues to debt reduction. The fourth is a Plant Nutrition segment that has turned from a USD 86.4 million operating loss in fiscal 2024 to USD 20.8 million of operating income in the nine months to June 2026, which diversifies earnings away from weather. The fifth is an improving earnings base: adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 233.2 million over the last twelve months. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 9–13; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F10

facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Compass Minerals produces rock salt, evaporated salt and magnesium chloride for road deicing, consumer and industrial uses, and sulfate of potash fertilizer, operating mines in Ontario, Louisiana and Cheshire and a solar evaporation plant in Utah. Salt is about 82% of sales, and highway deicing alone is about 63% of Salt segment sales, sold mostly through annual government tenders. The credit link is that demand for salt has no known cost-effective substitute for most high-volume uses, which gives cash-flow visibility on volumes in an average winter, but the same sales are weather-driven and seasonal, with salt earnings concentrated in the December and March quarters and cash flow in the first half of the calendar year, so liquidity preservation and the revolver matter more than annual averages. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Compass Minerals International, Inc. is a Delaware holding company whose subsidiaries conduct all operations, so creditors of the parent notes depend on subsidiary cash flows and on guarantees from certain unnamed domestic subsidiaries; the revolver is secured on substantially all U.S. assets, the Goderich mine and stock of certain subsidiaries, and the receivables facility sits in a separate special purpose subsidiary whose assets are not available to other creditors. There is no sponsor or controlling shareholder in the filings; Koch held about 17% after its 2022 placement, with the current holding not supplied. The credit implication is that distribution and exit pressure from an owner is absent, but so is a committed source of equity support, and structural priority between the secured revolver, the receivables facility and the unsecured notes cannot be fully read without the executed documents. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue follows volume times price. Highway volumes depend on snowfall and are sold through annual tenders and some multi-year contracts, with about 75% of UK highway customers on multi-year contracts, so price is set once a year while volume is known only after the winter; consumer and industrial salt, 37% of Salt segment sales, is steadier and higher priced. No customer or affiliated group exceeded 10% of sales in the last three fiscal years. Plant Nutrition sells sulfate of potash, which commands a premium to muriate of potash, mostly to U.S. customers (88%), and its average price rose 10.16% in the nine months to June 2026. The revenue is therefore predictable in direction but cyclical in size, exposed to weather and, for sulfate of potash, to imports and commodity potash; the creditor consequence is that one winter's revenue is a poor guide to coverage and the prudent reading uses a multi-year average. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 12–16; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 158; calculation F4

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Costs are dominated by product cost (57.07% of fiscal 2025 sales) and shipping and handling (27.60%), with selling, general and administrative cost at 9.11% after a reduction of USD 24.5 million in fiscal 2025. Mining and processing carry a large fixed element and are energy-intensive (electricity, diesel and natural gas), freight depends on distance and fuel, and about half of the workforce is unionised, so operating leverage is high: lower volume raises cost per ton, and inflation in freight or labour is hard to offset until the next tender. Management expects production costs to stay elevated near term and says mine-level costs have not yet improved at the pace expected. Margins can be defended against modest cost inflation through pricing gains, as the 7.80% highway price rise shows, but not against a combined volume and cost shock, so creditors should treat the 18.05% adjusted EBITDA margin as a good-winter margin. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation F4

facts.label: Capital intensity and FCF conversion
facts.text: Capital expenditure was USD 114.2 million in fiscal 2024, USD 69.7 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 62.1 million in the nine months to June 2026, with fiscal 2026 guidance of USD 90 million to USD 110 million; no split between maintenance and growth is stated, so flexibility cannot be measured. Cash interest paid was USD 59.3 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 41.6 million over the last twelve months, cash taxes were USD 38.5 million over the last twelve months, and working capital swings with inventory, which released USD 87.3 million in fiscal 2025. The result is that free cash flow of USD 77.9 million over the last twelve months is about 0.33x adjusted EBITDA, enough to repay debt gradually but not to retire the 2030 notes, which means refinancing will be needed. Capital spending can be cut as it was in fiscal 2025 (down 39.0%), which gives some protection in a downside, but cuts that defer mine maintenance would raise cost later. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F5; calculation F11

facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is strong: salt is a commodity, competitors in North America include large nationally recognised companies and regional producers, and two competitors serve the UK highway market, so price competes within delivered cost and the company's depots, Great Lakes position and deep-water port are its edge; creditors should expect price gains to be contested. Entry barriers differ: the filing says they are low in consumer and industrial salt, and, as an analyst reading rather than a company statement, they are high for rock salt mining because few mines combine scale and port access. Substitutes are weak for high-volume uses by management's account, and for sulfate of potash the substitute is muriate of potash, which is cheaper but contains chloride. Buyer power is high in highway deicing because government buyers tender annually, and low in sulfate of potash where the company is the only North American producer. Supplier power matters through energy, freight and, for some products, purchased potassium chloride and calcium chloride, with natural gas partly hedged. The net effect on credit is that pricing power is moderate and cost pass-through slow, which supports the view of volatile but recoverable margins. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 11–16; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 131–132

facts.label: PEST analysis
facts.text: Only three factors change credit outcomes. Political and regulatory: U.S. tariffs of up to 50% on certain Canadian imports were announced for August 19, 2026, and Canadian mines supply U.S. highway customers, but the company reports its products are compliant with the United States-Mexico-Canada trade agreement and its Canadian exports were previously exempt, so the effect is not quantified and could affect Goderich margins; Utah rule-making on the Great Salt Lake may affect extraction at Ogden, which underpins sulfate of potash and solar salt output. Economic: freight, fuel and labour inflation and interest rates bear on cost and on the revolver rate of about 5.8%. Social and technological factors are not credit drivers on the filings read. The consequence is that the Canadian tariff outcome and Ogden's lake access are monitoring items, not conclusions. facts.label: SWOT analysis
facts.text: Strengths: scale and port-linked logistics at Goderich, near-term maturity clearance, aligned financial policy, Plant Nutrition recovery and a rating upgrade, each supporting debt service. Weaknesses: weather dependence, mine concentration, interest burden, single 2030 maturity and weak reporting controls, each constraining cash flow or visibility. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: pricing momentum in highway bids, further debt reduction from free cash flow, refinancing the 2030 notes after the first call date at a lower coupon, and mine efficiency gains that management has not yet delivered. Threats that could weaken credit quality: a mild winter, freight and labour inflation, tariffs on Canadian exports, loss of Goderich output, a change in dividend policy and a failure to remediate control weaknesses. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 176

facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Business scale and market position are average: the company leads in North American sulfate of potash and operates the largest underground salt mine in the world, but sells commodities and has USD 1,292.1 million of last-twelve-month revenue. Competitive advantage is average: logistics and asset quality help, but there is little differentiation. Diversification is weak: two product families, one mine for about half of salt tons and weather exposure dominate. Cost and capex flexibility is average: spending has been cut but costs are largely fixed and logistics-driven. Margin stability is weak to average: the adjusted EBITDA margin moved from 18.46% in fiscal 2024 to 15.98% in fiscal 2025 and 18.05% over the last twelve months. Free cash flow stability is weak: negative in fiscal 2024, positive since, with seasonal and inventory effects. Ability to refinance is average: a single 2030 bond at a high coupon, no maturity before 2028, and a recent rating upgrade reported by the company. Liquidity is average to strong against near-term obligations but flattered by the seasonal low. Financial policy and governance is average: aligned in behaviour but with weak controls. The credit supports are leverage near 3x, clear maturities and aligned policy; the constraints are volatility, concentration and interest burden; the trend is improving; the missing data are covenant definitions, peers and the fiscal 2026 year end. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F1; calculation F5

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: In the next 12 to 24 months management guides fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA to USD 218 million to USD 242 million with a USD 230 million midpoint, capital expenditure to USD 90 million to USD 110 million and net interest expense to USD 62 million to USD 67 million, and says fiscal 2027 demand should be lower than fiscal 2026 on normal weather after a stronger-than-average winter. Guidance and nine-month results imply a fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 38.4 million at the midpoint against USD 41.6 million a year earlier. Tailwinds are the constructive bid season, Plant Nutrition momentum and lower debt. Headwinds are volume normalisation, cost inflation, tariffs and the 2028 revolver. Over three to five years the issue is refinancing the 2030 notes, callable from July 2027 at 104.0% and at par from July 2029, and keeping leverage low enough to do so; sector demand for salt grows slowly (flat to about 1% a year by management's estimate) while prices have risen about 3% to 4% a year, which supports modest growth only. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario replays fiscal 2024, the issuer's own weak-winter year. The initiating condition is a mild 2026-27 winter in which highway volumes fall by about the 16.95% by which fiscal 2024 volumes trailed fiscal 2025, on top of the normalisation management already expects. The first operational break is unabsorbed fixed cost at the mines and unsold salt that raises inventory, as in fiscal 2024 when payables fell and inventory built. The financial transmission is lower Salt earnings and a working-capital build that turned operating cash flow to USD 14.4 million in fiscal 2024 and free cash flow to negative USD 99.8 million; the same result today would use about 30.42% of liquidity of USD 328.1 million, mainly through revolver borrowings. Leverage would rise because debt would not fall and adjusted EBITDA would decline, and the covenant tests and the revolver maturity in May 2028 would become more relevant. Management's levers are capital expenditure, inventory release, suspension of dividends already in place and asset sales. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in one such year because liquidity and the maturity profile are stronger than in fiscal 2024, and the observable triggers are revolver borrowings above USD 35.0 million at a seasonal low, a December quarter working-capital build and adjusted EBITDA below the guidance range. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 125 and 141–142; 10-K_2024-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 128; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F7

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Compass Minerals presents an adequate business profile supported by the scale and port-linked logistics of the Goderich mine, a recovering Plant Nutrition segment and aligned financial policy, but credit quality is constrained by weather dependence, mine concentration and an 8.00% bond that makes interest the heaviest fixed claim. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in an average winter and weak in a mild one, because free cash flow is seasonal and was negative in fiscal 2024. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage staying near 3x and on market access in 2027 and 2028, before the revolver falls due in May 2028. The primary downside path is a mild winter with cost inflation that builds inventory and draws the revolver. Further analysis would require the covenant definitions and compliance certificates, the executed documents, the fiscal 2026 annual report and a peer set. The review is complete with limitations, and the top risk is weather-driven earnings volatility. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F1; calculation F7

## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied filings and releases support Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit only as of the quarter ended June 30, 2026, 141 days before the as-of date, so any creditor conclusion describes that balance sheet.
Basis: calculation C1; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 57

Five limits shape how far the work can be trusted. The fiscal year that ended September 30, 2026 and any event after the August 6, 2026 quarterly report are not covered. No executed credit agreement or indenture is supplied, and the March and June 2026 quarterly reports print no covenant compliance statement, so covenant headroom is not established beyond the September 2025 ratio. The company reports that its internal control weaknesses are still being remediated, and its filings give two different maturity dates for the 2030 notes.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage fell to 3.31x reported EBITDA at June 30, 2026 from 7.05x at September 30, 2025, but much of that drop is a fiscal 2025 impairment leaving the base, so creditors should underwrite the adjusted 3.07x, not a finished repair. On adjusted EBITDA the move is smaller, from 4.19x to 3.07x.
Basis: calculation K20; calculation K22; calculation K37; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 139

Debt on the company's definition is USD 716.6 million and net debt is USD 660.3 million. Of USD 728.0 million of principal, USD 650.0 million falls due in 2030 and nothing falls due before 2028. Cash interest cover of 5.21x flatters, because the last twelve months hold one coupon on the 2030 notes, not two; cover on interest expense is 3.19x. Liquidity of USD 328.1 million is struck at the seasonal low for working-capital needs.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 45; EX99.1_2026-06-30_cmp_cmp-q32026earningsreleasee-htm.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation K7; calculation K8; calculation K13; calculation K14; calculation K24; calculation K26; calculation K27
### Leverage trajectory and drivers

Leverage on the company's own debt definition fell in two steps. Total debt, which is long-term debt net of financing costs and excludes finance leases, went from USD 917.5 million at September 30, 2024 to USD 832.2 million a year later and USD 716.6 million at June 30, 2026, while last-twelve-month reported EBITDA moved from negative USD 13.7 million in fiscal 2024 to USD 118.0 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 216.6 million. Reported EBITDA carries non-cash charges, USD 191.0 million of impairments in fiscal 2024 and USD 53.7 million in fiscal 2025, so reported leverage is not calculable for fiscal 2024 and is 7.05x for fiscal 2025. Taking only the fiscal 2025 impairment out of EBITDA would give 4.85x, so about 2.20x of the 3.74x fall to 3.31x is that charge leaving the base, and the rest is debt paydown and earnings growth. On the issuer-adjusted measure, which adds the charges back, gross leverage was 4.45x, 4.19x and 3.07x and net leverage at June 30, 2026 is 2.83x, matching the company's own 2.8x. Creditors should therefore anchor on adjusted leverage near 3x and reported leverage near 3.3x, and treat any reading of a seven-turn improvement as an artefact of the base year.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 139; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-06-30_cmp_cmp-q32026earningsreleasee-htm.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K3; calculation K20; calculation K22; calculation K23; calculation K37

Debt reduction came from operations and a disposal, not from new equity. Operating cash flow was USD 197.7 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 162.8 million in the nine months to June 30, 2026, against capital expenditure of USD 69.7 million and USD 62.1 million, and the Wynyard sale added USD 23.3 million of net cash on March 1, 2026. The remaining USD 150.0 million of 6.75% notes was redeemed at par on March 30, 2026 while the revolver rose to USD 35.0 million and cash stayed near USD 56.3 million, so part of the paydown is a swap of note debt for revolver debt rather than a fall in every claim: total principal fell USD 117.8 million, less than the USD 150.0 million redeemed. The consequence for creditors is that near-term maturities are gone but the revolver, the most senior claim, is now partly drawn.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 141–142; calculation K9
### Coverage and cash interest

Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 1.99x in fiscal 2025 and 5.21x over the last twelve months, but the second figure overstates cover. The 2030 notes pay on January 1 and July 1 and their first coupon fell due on January 1, 2026, so the twelve months to June 30, 2026 hold one coupon, not two. Cash interest paid was USD 41.6 million against interest expense of USD 67.9 million, and the half-year coupon of USD 26.0 million fell due the day after the quarter end, with accrued interest of USD 26.4 million on the balance sheet. On interest expense, reported EBITDA covers 3.19x and adjusted EBITDA 3.43x. The 2030 notes alone cost USD 52.0 million a year in cash, so cash cover should be expected to fall back toward the expense-based figure once two coupons fall in a twelve-month window; creditors should use 3.19x.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 176; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation K13; calculation K14; calculation K24; calculation K26; calculation K27; calculation K40
### Cash-flow quality

Operating cash flow of USD 162.8 million in the nine months to June 30, 2026 included USD 40.4 million of working-capital release (receivables 26.6, inventories 40.1, other assets 33.2, payables negative 2.0, other liabilities negative 57.5), against USD 137.1 million in the same nine months a year earlier, when inventories alone released USD 138.0 million. Before working-capital changes it was USD 122.4 million, compared with USD 67.5 million, so earnings carry more of the cash flow than a year ago. The figure is still seasonal: management says working-capital needs are lowest in the June quarter and highest in the December quarter, so the nine-month cash flow and the June 30 net debt flatter the full-year position. Free cash flow (operating cash flow less capital expenditure) was negative USD 99.8 million in fiscal 2024, USD 128.0 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 77.9 million over the last twelve months, 0.33x adjusted EBITDA. Fiscal 2025 benefited from an inventory release of USD 87.3 million. Capital expenditure is a total only; no maintenance and growth split is stated, so the part of spending that is discretionary is not established.

### Liquidity and maturity profile

Liquidity is USD 328.1 million at June 30, 2026 (cash USD 56.3 million plus USD 271.8 million of undrawn revolver), against USD 364.6 million at September 30, 2025 and USD 189.9 million at September 30, 2024. The revolver (commitments of USD 325.0 million, borrowings of USD 35.0 million and letters of credit of USD 18.2 million) falls due in May 2028, about 22 months after the balance sheet date, and is the nearest maturity; the AR facility's USD 43.0 million follows in March 2029 and the USD 650.0 million 2030 notes after that, which is 89.29% of principal. No principal is due in fiscal 2026 or fiscal 2027. Refinancing risk is therefore not near, but one bullet carries almost nine-tenths of the debt and the revolver is the only committed backstop. The AR facility's undrawn capacity (up to USD 100.0 million, subject to conditions, with USD 43.0 million drawn) is not stated and is excluded, and USD 14.5 million of the cash is held by foreign subsidiaries. The 2030 notes become callable at 104.0% of principal from July 1, 2027, falling to par on or after July 1, 2029, so a refinancing before 2029 would carry a call premium of up to 4.0%.

### Strongest contrary evidence

The strongest case against caution is that the company's own measures are consistent and improving. Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 233.2 million over the last twelve months from USD 198.8 million in fiscal 2025, net leverage is 2.83x, S&P is reported by the company to have raised the rating to B+, and fiscal 2026 guidance of USD 218 million to USD 242 million (midpoint USD 230 million) implies earnings hold near the last-twelve-month level while the nearest maturity is 22 months away. That case wins if net leverage stays near 3x at the December 31, 2026 balance sheet, when working capital is at its seasonal high, and if cover on interest expense holds near 3.19x once two coupons fall in one twelve-month window. Caution wins if adjusted EBITDA slips below the guidance midpoint, if cash add-backs recur (restructuring of USD 4.3 million and recall costs of USD 2.1 million in fiscal 2025), or if revolver borrowings rise above USD 35.0 million at a seasonal low.

### Data quality and definition risks

Management reports material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting that are still being remediated, and the auditor gave an adverse opinion on internal control at September 30, 2024 and September 30, 2025, so the figures carry a reliability risk even though the auditor's opinion on the fiscal 2025 statements says they present fairly. The cross-checks that could be run agree: fiscal 2024 sales, net loss, EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and total debt are the same in the 2024 and 2025 annual reports, and the nine-month and quarter figures in the June 2026 quarterly report agree with the third-quarter release for sales, operating income, net income, EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and net debt. The differences found are presentational: finance leases moved to their own balance sheet lines and a term loan repayment was reclassified inside financing cash flows. Three debt bases coexist for one date (total debt of USD 716.6 million, principal of USD 728.0 million and carrying value with finance leases of USD 728.1 million), and the covenant tests use first lien debt at principal and a consolidated EBITDA that may include run-rate cost savings, neither of which is supplied, so no headroom is computed. The 2030 notes carry two maturity dates and two cost figures in the filings, and the debt table captions senior notes as subordinated, which is why ranking follows the notes' own description.

### Claims outside debt and events after the balance sheet date

Claims outside Total Debt are finance lease liabilities of USD 11.5 million on their own lines, operating lease liabilities of USD 46.5 million (USD 53.9 million at September 30, 2025) inside other liabilities, and letters of credit of USD 18.2 million that reduce revolver availability. The performance bonds of USD 157.4 million posted for the Canadian provincial tax dispute were released on its settlement in November 2025. No customer deposits, factoring or supplier finance programmes were found in the sources read, and deferred revenue is USD 0.5 million, so no non-debt funding float of credit relevance is identified. After June 30, 2026 the sources record the July 20, 2026 announcement of tariffs of up to 50% on certain Canadian imports, effective August 19, 2026, which bears on the company's exports from Canada into the United States (the filing says they were previously exempt); its effect is not quantified and it changes no period figure and no net debt figure.

### Gaps with the largest credit consequence

Three gaps matter most. The latest statements are 141 days old and the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 is not covered, so year-end net debt and leverage after the winter working-capital cycle are not established. Covenant compliance after December 31, 2025 is not established and the covenant EBITDA definition is not supplied, so headroom against the first lien net leverage test and the interest coverage test cannot be read. The AR facility's rank, rate and undrawn capacity are not stated, so USD 43.0 million of debt sits outside the ranking and the facility's possible further capacity sits outside liquidity. The full list is under Gaps.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Compass Minerals is a weather-exposed producer that depends on one large mine and a largely new management team, with no controlling sponsor behind it, so creditors rely on operating delivery and cash discipline, not owner support.
Basis: calculation B5; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 101–103; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 190

Salt supplies about 82% of sales, and the Goderich mine alone produced about half of the salt tonnage in fiscal 2025. Financial policy has been aligned with creditors since April 2024: no dividends, and disposal proceeds used with cash to retire debt. Governance remains the weak point, with unremediated control weaknesses and a new operations chief in August 2026, so sponsor and governance risk is Medium.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX99.1_2026-06-30_cmp_cmp-q32026earningsreleasee-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 53–55; EX99.1_2026-06-30_cmp_cmp-risnerex991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation B5; calculation B7
### Key findings

- Earnings follow winter weather, so volumes swing before prices can respond. Highway deicing volumes rose 20.41% in fiscal 2025 on a more normal winter and fell 2.54% in the nine months to June 2026, while the average highway price rose 7.80%. Highway sales are won mostly in annual government tenders, so a mild winter cuts volume at once and price can only recover at the next bid, which is why one winter's results should not be read as the run rate.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 110; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 125; EX99.1_2026-06-30_cmp_cmp-q32026earningsreleasee-htm.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation B10

- One mine carries the portfolio, which concentrates operating and labour risk. Goderich produced 50.29% of fiscal 2025 salt tonnage, nearly half of the workforce is under collective agreements, and a new three-year Goderich agreement was announced in May 2026, which removes the nearest labour deadline at that site.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 63; EX99.1_2026-03-31_cmp_cmp-q22026earningsreleasee-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation B5

- Plant Nutrition has moved from loss to contributor but is small and smaller after the Wynyard sale. Segment operating income was USD 20.8 million in the nine months to June 2026 against USD 0.3 million a year earlier and an operating loss of USD 86.4 million in fiscal 2024, so the segment now supports cash flow instead of draining it, though one site at Ogden now provides all its capacity.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 187–188; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9

- No sponsor extracts value, and the largest identified holder is a strategic minority. Koch owned about 17% at the October 2022 placement, current holdings are not established, the board stopped dividends in April 2024 after a USD 12.6 million payment in fiscal 2024, and no management, monitoring or advisory fees to an owner are disclosed. This corrects Source readiness, which found no significant shareholder named in the filings.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 190; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 141; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 28; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Governance is the weak point because reporting quality has not yet been re-established. Material weaknesses first reported with a restatement are still being remediated, the auditor gave an adverse opinion on internal control at both year ends, every listed executive officer took the current post between January 2024 and September 2025, and one has already left, so creditors lean on figures and a team without a long record.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 101–103; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 53–55; EX99.1_2026-06-30_cmp_cmp-risnerex991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

- Transactions since 2024 are repair, not expansion. Management ended the lithium project, exited Fortress (sold for USD 20.0 million), refinanced with USD 650.0 million of notes, sold Wynyard for cash proceeds of USD 23.3 million and redeemed the last USD 150.0 million of 2027 notes, which shows creditor-aligned priorities but also a record of capital lost on projects outside the core.
Basis: 10-K_2024-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 156; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 8–11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15

- Unit cost is the lever management has not yet delivered. Shipping and handling cost is 27.60% of fiscal 2025 sales, management says mine-level costs are improving but not at the pace it expected, and it expects production costs to stay elevated, so the pricing gains in the salt segment can be consumed by cost before they reach creditors.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_cmp_cmp-q22026earningsreleasee-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-06-30_cmp_cmp-q32026earningsreleasee-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation B6
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is that, in management's words, salt has no known cost-effective alternative for most high-volume uses, that no customer reached 10% of sales in any of the last three fiscal years, that highway prices rose 7.80% in the nine months to June 2026 and management describes the coming highway bid season as constructive, and that Plant Nutrition earnings have recovered. Management also reports a stronger-than-average winter in fiscal 2026. These support a view that the business is steadier than its weather exposure suggests. The view would improve if the next winter is average and the fiscal 2027 volume decline management expects is mild, if remediation of the control weaknesses is reported complete, and if Goderich production costs fall. It would worsen if a mine or labour disruption hits Goderich, if the tariffs announced for August 2026 reach Canadian salt exports, or if the board reverses the dividend suspension before debt is lower.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 158; EX99.1_2026-06-30_cmp_cmp-q32026earningsreleasee-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation B10

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No new debt issue or acquisition is reported after June 30, 2026 in the documents read. The transactions that shape the creditor position are all earlier. On June 16, 2025 the company issued USD 650.0 million of 8.00% senior unsecured notes due 2030 and used the proceeds to repay the revolver and term loan in full and to redeem USD 350.0 million of its 6.75% notes due 2027; the same day a fifth amendment fixed revolver commitments at USD 325.0 million and reset the financial covenants to a first lien leverage test and an interest coverage test. On March 30, 2026 it redeemed the remaining USD 150.0 million of the 2027 notes at par from cash, and on March 19, 2026 it extended its receivables financing facility to March 2029. On March 1, 2026 it sold the Wynyard sulfate of potash business for total consideration of about USD 30.8 million, receiving USD 23.3 million of net cash and booking a USD 14.5 million loss, of which USD 13.1 million is non-cash. In 2025 it exited the Fortress fire retardant business it had bought in 2023, selling the assets for USD 20.0 million, and in January 2024 it ended its lithium project after an impairment of USD 74.8 million. For creditors, the sequence moved the company from secured bank debt and subordinated notes to a structure dominated by one unsecured bond due 2030, with a small revolver and receivables facility, removed near-term maturities and stopped capital going to projects outside salt and sulfate of potash.

### Overall governance view

Overall, Compass Minerals presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is the suspension of dividends in April 2024 and the use of asset-sale proceeds and cash to retire notes, which matters because it keeps cash in the business and lowers refinancing exposure, and implies a financial policy aligned with creditors. Countervailing evidence is the unremediated control weaknesses, a restatement, a notice of default in September 2024 for a late quarterly report that was cured, and a management team in which every listed officer took the current post since January 2024. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit agreement and indenture, and the fiscal 2026 annual report. The review is complete with limitations at a Medium risk level.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Compass Minerals' fundamental credit profile is adequate but fragile: adjusted leverage of 3.07x and no maturity before 2028 support creditors, but weather-driven earnings, one dominant mine and a new management team mean one weak winter could reverse the gains.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F1; calculation F2

Cash interest cover of 5.21x overstates strength, because the last twelve months hold one coupon on the 2030 notes; cover on interest expense is 3.19x, and USD 650.0 million of USD 728.0 million of principal falls due in 2030. Liquidity of USD 328.1 million is struck at the seasonal low for working-capital needs. The primary downside is a mild winter with unit-cost inflation, which would be absorbed by liquidity before it threatens a covenant or a maturity.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 176; calculation F1; calculation F3; calculation F9
### Key findings

- Revenue is steady in demand but volatile in volume, which makes earnings lumpy rather than fragile. Highway deicing volumes rose 20.41% in fiscal 2025 and fell 2.54% in the nine months to June 2026 while the average highway price rose 7.80%, and prices reset only at annual tenders, so a mild winter cuts volume at once and price can recover only a year later. Creditors should underwrite the average of several winters, not the latest.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation F4

- Margins depend on freight and mine costs, which management has not yet brought down. Shipping and handling cost is 27.60% of sales and the company says mine-level costs are improving but not at the pace expected, so price increases in the salt segment can be absorbed by cost before they reach cash flow. The adjusted EBITDA margin was 18.05% over the last twelve months against 15.98% in fiscal 2025.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-06-30_cmp_cmp-q32026earningsreleasee-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation F4

- Cash conversion is adequate but helped by working capital. Free cash flow was USD 77.9 million over the last twelve months, 0.33x adjusted EBITDA, after negative USD 99.8 million in fiscal 2024 and USD 128.0 million in fiscal 2025 when an inventory release of USD 87.3 million helped, so conversion depends on the winter cycle and capital spending, which management is holding to a guided range.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F5

- Leverage is moderate and falling but rests on adjusted earnings. Net debt is USD 660.3 million, which is 2.83x adjusted EBITDA and 3.05x reported EBITDA, and the interest burden is high because the 8.00% notes cost about USD 52.0 million a year in cash, so interest cover on expense of 3.19x leaves limited room for an earnings miss.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F1; calculation F3; calculation F6

- Liquidity and refinancing are adequate near term and concentrated later. Liquidity of USD 328.1 million covers the revolver draw of USD 35.0 million, no principal falls due in fiscal 2026 or 2027, and the revolver is due in May 2028, but 89.29% of principal is a single 2030 bond that is callable at 104.0% from July 2027, so refinancing capacity depends on market access in 2027 and 2028.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 176; calculation F9

- Governance and financial policy support creditors but are untested. There is no sponsor, dividends have been suspended since April 2024, and asset sales and cash retired the 2027 notes, but control weaknesses remain and every listed executive officer took the current post in the last three years, so a new weakness would be hard to detect early.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

- The primary downside is a mild winter that coincides with cost inflation and a working-capital build. A fiscal 2024-type winter would cut highway volumes by 16.95% against fiscal 2025, and a repeat of fiscal 2024 free cash flow would use about 30.42% of today's liquidity, so the issuer has room to absorb one such year but not two in a row.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 125; calculation F7
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against calling the profile fragile is that adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 233.2 million over the last twelve months, that the company reports first lien net leverage of about 0.01x at September 30, 2025 against a covenant maximum that was 2.75x then and is 2.50x now, that S&P is reported to have raised the rating to B+ with adjusted leverage of 3.1x, that management describes the coming highway bid season as constructive, and that guidance of USD 218 million to USD 242 million implies earnings hold near the current level. These points make a stable view plausible. The view would improve if net leverage on reported EBITDA stays at or below 3.05x at the December 31, 2026 balance sheet, when working capital peaks, if remediation of the control weaknesses is reported complete, and if the revolver is extended before May 2027. It would worsen if the fiscal 2026 fourth quarter falls below the guidance midpoint implied for it, if revolver borrowings rise above USD 35.0 million at a seasonal low, or if Goderich output is interrupted.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX99.1_2026-06-30_cmp_cmp-q32026earningsreleasee-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation F1; calculation F8; calculation F12
### Limitations

- Covenant EBITDA and compliance after December 31, 2025 are not supplied, so the conclusion that covenants are not the near-term constraint rests on the first lien ratio reported at September 30, 2025 and on the debt now outstanding, not on a current calculation.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2025-12-31_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 11
- No peer set, market quotes or agency report is supplied, so the view that the business profile is adequate is an absolute reading and cannot be placed against other leveraged issuers.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The winter of fiscal 2027 and the fiscal 2026 year end are not covered, so the downside scenario is a replay of the fiscal 2024 outcome, not a forecast, and the size of a real shock could be smaller or larger.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 125; calculation F7
- Management's guidance and statements about cost improvement are its own, so the reading that earnings hold near the current level depends on delivery that is not independently supported.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_cmp_cmp-q32026earningsreleasee-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. The first strength is a low-cost, high-scale salt franchise. The Goderich mine is described as the largest underground rock salt mine in the world, with a deep-water port, and the company has logistics depots close to its customers, so delivered cost is competitive in a product where freight is a large part of price; this lowers the risk of losing tenders and supports volume through weak winters. The second strength is near-term refinancing safety: no principal falls due before May 2028 and liquidity is USD 328.1 million, so a poor quarter can be absorbed without a financing event. The third is financial policy: dividends are suspended and disposal proceeds and cash retired the 2027 notes, so cash accrues to debt reduction. The fourth is a Plant Nutrition segment that has turned from a USD 86.4 million operating loss in fiscal 2024 to USD 20.8 million of operating income in the nine months to June 2026, which diversifies earnings away from weather. The fifth is an improving earnings base: adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 233.2 million over the last twelve months.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 9–13; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F10

Weaknesses. The first weakness is weather dependence with an annual price cycle, so volume shocks hit earnings at once and price offsets arrive late. The second is concentration: Goderich produced 50.29% of fiscal 2025 salt tonnage, so a single-site disruption would remove about half of salt output. The third is interest burden: the 8.00% notes cost about USD 52.0 million a year, and cover on interest expense is 3.19x, so cost or volume misses have a fast effect on cash flow after interest. The fourth is a single large maturity, with 89.29% of principal due in 2030, which makes refinancing access in 2027 and 2028 the key test. The fifth is governance and reporting quality, with unremediated control weaknesses and a new management team, which raises the risk that figures or execution disappoint.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 12; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F3; calculation F6; calculation F9

### Company description

Compass Minerals produces rock salt, evaporated salt and magnesium chloride for road deicing, consumer and industrial uses, and sulfate of potash fertilizer, operating mines in Ontario, Louisiana and Cheshire and a solar evaporation plant in Utah. Salt is about 82% of sales, and highway deicing alone is about 63% of Salt segment sales, sold mostly through annual government tenders. The credit link is that demand for salt has no known cost-effective substitute for most high-volume uses, which gives cash-flow visibility on volumes in an average winter, but the same sales are weather-driven and seasonal, with salt earnings concentrated in the December and March quarters and cash flow in the first half of the calendar year, so liquidity preservation and the revolver matter more than annual averages. The company exited a fire retardant acquisition in 2025, ended a lithium project in January 2024 and sold its Wynyard sulfate of potash plant in March 2026, so the business that remains is narrower and more focused than it was three years ago.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 9–13; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 130
### Ownership and group structure

Compass Minerals International, Inc. is a Delaware holding company whose subsidiaries conduct all operations, so creditors of the parent notes depend on subsidiary cash flows and on guarantees from certain unnamed domestic subsidiaries; the revolver is secured on substantially all U.S. assets, the Goderich mine and stock of certain subsidiaries, and the receivables facility sits in a separate special purpose subsidiary whose assets are not available to other creditors. There is no sponsor or controlling shareholder in the filings; Koch held about 17% after its 2022 placement, with the current holding not supplied. The credit implication is that distribution and exit pressure from an owner is absent, but so is a committed source of equity support, and structural priority between the secured revolver, the receivables facility and the unsecured notes cannot be fully read without the executed documents.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 13–16; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 190
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue follows volume times price. Highway volumes depend on snowfall and are sold through annual tenders and some multi-year contracts, with about 75% of UK highway customers on multi-year contracts, so price is set once a year while volume is known only after the winter; consumer and industrial salt, 37% of Salt segment sales, is steadier and higher priced. No customer or affiliated group exceeded 10% of sales in the last three fiscal years. Plant Nutrition sells sulfate of potash, which commands a premium to muriate of potash, mostly to U.S. customers (88%), and its average price rose 10.16% in the nine months to June 2026. The revenue is therefore predictable in direction but cyclical in size, exposed to weather and, for sulfate of potash, to imports and commodity potash; the creditor consequence is that one winter's revenue is a poor guide to coverage and the prudent reading uses a multi-year average.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 12–16; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 158; calculation F4
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are dominated by product cost (57.07% of fiscal 2025 sales) and shipping and handling (27.60%), with selling, general and administrative cost at 9.11% after a reduction of USD 24.5 million in fiscal 2025. Mining and processing carry a large fixed element and are energy-intensive (electricity, diesel and natural gas), freight depends on distance and fuel, and about half of the workforce is unionised, so operating leverage is high: lower volume raises cost per ton, and inflation in freight or labour is hard to offset until the next tender. Management expects production costs to stay elevated near term and says mine-level costs have not yet improved at the pace expected. Margins can be defended against modest cost inflation through pricing gains, as the 7.80% highway price rise shows, but not against a combined volume and cost shock, so creditors should treat the 18.05% adjusted EBITDA margin as a good-winter margin.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation F4
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Capital expenditure was USD 114.2 million in fiscal 2024, USD 69.7 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 62.1 million in the nine months to June 2026, with fiscal 2026 guidance of USD 90 million to USD 110 million; no split between maintenance and growth is stated, so flexibility cannot be measured. Cash interest paid was USD 59.3 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 41.6 million over the last twelve months, cash taxes were USD 38.5 million over the last twelve months, and working capital swings with inventory, which released USD 87.3 million in fiscal 2025. The result is that free cash flow of USD 77.9 million over the last twelve months is about 0.33x adjusted EBITDA, enough to repay debt gradually but not to retire the 2030 notes, which means refinancing will be needed. Capital spending can be cut as it was in fiscal 2025 (down 39.0%), which gives some protection in a downside, but cuts that defer mine maintenance would raise cost later.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F5; calculation F11
### Porter's five forces

Competitive rivalry is strong: salt is a commodity, competitors in North America include large nationally recognised companies and regional producers, and two competitors serve the UK highway market, so price competes within delivered cost and the company's depots, Great Lakes position and deep-water port are its edge; creditors should expect price gains to be contested. Entry barriers differ: the filing says they are low in consumer and industrial salt, and, as an analyst reading rather than a company statement, they are high for rock salt mining because few mines combine scale and port access. Substitutes are weak for high-volume uses by management's account, and for sulfate of potash the substitute is muriate of potash, which is cheaper but contains chloride. Buyer power is high in highway deicing because government buyers tender annually, and low in sulfate of potash where the company is the only North American producer. Supplier power matters through energy, freight and, for some products, purchased potassium chloride and calcium chloride, with natural gas partly hedged. The net effect on credit is that pricing power is moderate and cost pass-through slow, which supports the view of volatile but recoverable margins.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 11–16; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 131–132
### PEST analysis

Only three factors change credit outcomes. Political and regulatory: U.S. tariffs of up to 50% on certain Canadian imports were announced for August 19, 2026, and Canadian mines supply U.S. highway customers, but the company reports its products are compliant with the United States-Mexico-Canada trade agreement and its Canadian exports were previously exempt, so the effect is not quantified and could affect Goderich margins; Utah rule-making on the Great Salt Lake may affect extraction at Ogden, which underpins sulfate of potash and solar salt output. Economic: freight, fuel and labour inflation and interest rates bear on cost and on the revolver rate of about 5.8%. Social and technological factors are not credit drivers on the filings read. The consequence is that the Canadian tariff outcome and Ogden's lake access are monitoring items, not conclusions.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 44 and 71–72; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 14
### SWOT analysis

Strengths: scale and port-linked logistics at Goderich, near-term maturity clearance, aligned financial policy, Plant Nutrition recovery and a rating upgrade, each supporting debt service. Weaknesses: weather dependence, mine concentration, interest burden, single 2030 maturity and weak reporting controls, each constraining cash flow or visibility. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: pricing momentum in highway bids, further debt reduction from free cash flow, refinancing the 2030 notes after the first call date at a lower coupon, and mine efficiency gains that management has not yet delivered. Threats that could weaken credit quality: a mild winter, freight and labour inflation, tariffs on Canadian exports, loss of Goderich output, a change in dividend policy and a failure to remediate control weaknesses.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 176
### Financial profile and credit quality

Business scale and market position are average: the company leads in North American sulfate of potash and operates the largest underground salt mine in the world, but sells commodities and has USD 1,292.1 million of last-twelve-month revenue. Competitive advantage is average: logistics and asset quality help, but there is little differentiation. Diversification is weak: two product families, one mine for about half of salt tons and weather exposure dominate. Cost and capex flexibility is average: spending has been cut but costs are largely fixed and logistics-driven. Margin stability is weak to average: the adjusted EBITDA margin moved from 18.46% in fiscal 2024 to 15.98% in fiscal 2025 and 18.05% over the last twelve months. Free cash flow stability is weak: negative in fiscal 2024, positive since, with seasonal and inventory effects. Ability to refinance is average: a single 2030 bond at a high coupon, no maturity before 2028, and a recent rating upgrade reported by the company. Liquidity is average to strong against near-term obligations but flattered by the seasonal low. Financial policy and governance is average: aligned in behaviour but with weak controls. The credit supports are leverage near 3x, clear maturities and aligned policy; the constraints are volatility, concentration and interest burden; the trend is improving; the missing data are covenant definitions, peers and the fiscal 2026 year end.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F1; calculation F5
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

In the next 12 to 24 months management guides fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA to USD 218 million to USD 242 million with a USD 230 million midpoint, capital expenditure to USD 90 million to USD 110 million and net interest expense to USD 62 million to USD 67 million, and says fiscal 2027 demand should be lower than fiscal 2026 on normal weather after a stronger-than-average winter. Guidance and nine-month results imply a fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 38.4 million at the midpoint against USD 41.6 million a year earlier. Tailwinds are the constructive bid season, Plant Nutrition momentum and lower debt. Headwinds are volume normalisation, cost inflation, tariffs and the 2028 revolver. Over three to five years the issue is refinancing the 2030 notes, callable from July 2027 at 104.0% and at par from July 2029, and keeping leverage low enough to do so; sector demand for salt grows slowly (flat to about 1% a year by management's estimate) while prices have risen about 3% to 4% a year, which supports modest growth only.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_cmp_cmp-q32026earningsreleasee-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 11 and 176; calculation F8
### Qualitative downside scenario

The scenario replays fiscal 2024, the issuer's own weak-winter year. The initiating condition is a mild 2026-27 winter in which highway volumes fall by about the 16.95% by which fiscal 2024 volumes trailed fiscal 2025, on top of the normalisation management already expects. The first operational break is unabsorbed fixed cost at the mines and unsold salt that raises inventory, as in fiscal 2024 when payables fell and inventory built. The financial transmission is lower Salt earnings and a working-capital build that turned operating cash flow to USD 14.4 million in fiscal 2024 and free cash flow to negative USD 99.8 million; the same result today would use about 30.42% of liquidity of USD 328.1 million, mainly through revolver borrowings. Leverage would rise because debt would not fall and adjusted EBITDA would decline, and the covenant tests and the revolver maturity in May 2028 would become more relevant. Management's levers are capital expenditure, inventory release, suspension of dividends already in place and asset sales. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in one such year because liquidity and the maturity profile are stronger than in fiscal 2024, and the observable triggers are revolver borrowings above USD 35.0 million at a seasonal low, a December quarter working-capital build and adjusted EBITDA below the guidance range.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, pages 125 and 141–142; 10-K_2024-09-30_cmp.htm.jsonl, page 128; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F7
### Overall credit view

Overall, Compass Minerals presents an adequate business profile supported by the scale and port-linked logistics of the Goderich mine, a recovering Plant Nutrition segment and aligned financial policy, but credit quality is constrained by weather dependence, mine concentration and an 8.00% bond that makes interest the heaviest fixed claim. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in an average winter and weak in a mild one, because free cash flow is seasonal and was negative in fiscal 2024. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage staying near 3x and on market access in 2027 and 2028, before the revolver falls due in May 2028. The primary downside path is a mild winter with cost inflation that builds inventory and draws the revolver. Further analysis would require the covenant definitions and compliance certificates, the executed documents, the fiscal 2026 annual report and a peer set. The review is complete with limitations, and the top risk is weather-driven earnings volatility.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F1; calculation F7

## Gaps

- Covenant compliance after December 31, 2025 and the covenant definition of EBITDA are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculated and the covenant levels are shown only as monitoring signals. Severity: Medium. Closing action: supply compliance certificates and the executed credit agreement.

- No peer set, market quote or agency report is supplied, so the profile is judged in absolute terms and the rating upgrade is company-reported only. Severity: Medium. Closing action: supply peer financials and the agency report.

- The fiscal 2026 year end, the winter inventory position and any later management or ownership change are not covered, so the downside is a replay of fiscal 2024, not a forecast. Severity: Medium. Closing action: supply the fiscal 2026 annual report.

- The receivables facility's undrawn capacity, rate, rank and security detail are not stated, so liquidity excludes it and structural priority among the revolver, receivables facility and unsecured notes is not established. Severity: Medium. Closing action: supply the receivables financing agreement and the indenture.
- Capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, so the flexibility of spending in a downside is not measured. Severity: Low. Closing action: management disclosure.

- Mine-level costs, margins and reserve life are not stated, so the earnings weight of the Goderich mine is not established beyond its share of tons. Severity: Low. Closing action: mine technical reports.
- The effect of the tariffs announced for August 2026 on Canadian salt exports is not quantified, so it is a monitoring signal, not a conclusion. Severity: Low. Closing action: company disclosure.

- Quantitative thresholds for sector deterioration are not supported by the documents read, so the monitoring signal for weather is qualitative. Severity: Low. Closing action: set an internal snowfall measure.

- Financial foundation's cash cover of 5.21x uses one coupon on the 2030 notes in the twelve months; this module uses cover on interest expense for its reading and states both. Severity: Low. Closing action: re-measure after the fiscal 2026 annual report.

- Source readiness recorded no significant shareholder; Business & governance corrected this with Koch's 2022 stake and this module uses the corrected reading, with the current holding not supplied. Severity: Low. Closing action: supply the proxy statement.
